# gluestack config

`npm run design:gen` compiles the registries into
`components/ui/gluestack-ui-provider/config.ts`:

```ts
// Generated by design/tools/sources/generate.py -- do not edit by hand.
// Source of truth: design/tokens.xml + design/themes.xml
import { vars } from 'nativewind';

export const colors = {
  light: {
    '--background': '250 250 250',
    '--primary': '37 99 235',
    '--primary-foreground': '255 255 255',
    // ...
  },
  dark: {
    '--background': '24 24 27',
    '--primary': '59 130 246',
    '--primary-foreground': '255 255 255',
    // ...
  },
};

export const config = {
  light: vars(colors.light),
  dark: vars(colors.dark),
};
```

The provider (`components/ui/gluestack-ui-provider`) applies `config[mode]`, and
`useGluestackColors()` converts each space-separated triplet back to hex when a
library needs a literal colour.

To change a colour: edit `design/themes.xml` (or the palette in
`design/tokens.xml`) and run `npm run design:gen`.

## Design tokens

The second generated artifact is `components/ui/gluestack-ui-provider/tokens.js`.
It is the **entire** Tailwind theme: `tailwind.config.js` contains no design
value at all, it only does `extend: tokens.theme`. So the XML registries are the
single source of truth for the gluestack/nativewind theme.

In a consuming project, that same theme is published as
`@flipova/foundation/tokens` - see [Installation](/docs/getting-started/installation) for the three-line setup.

Two inputs feed it:

- **semantic colours**, one per `themes.xml` role, bound to the CSS variables
  emitted in `config.ts` (this is what keeps `bg-primary/50` working);
- **scale tokens**, from `design/tokens.xml`.

```js
module.exports = {
  theme: {
    colors: {
      primary: 'rgb(var(--primary)/<alpha-value>)',
      'primary-foreground': 'rgb(var(--primary-foreground)/<alpha-value>)',
      success: 'rgb(var(--success)/<alpha-value>)',
      // ... one entry per themes.xml role
    },
    spacing: { '0': '0px', '1': '4px', '4': '16px' },
    borderRadius: { 'sm': '4px', 'md': '8px', 'full': '9999px' },
    screens: { 'xs': '480px', 'sm': '640px', 'md': '768px' },
    fontFamily: {
      system: ['system-ui', '-apple-system', 'sans-serif'],
      body: ['var(--font-sans)'],
      roboto: ['Roboto', 'sans-serif'],
    },
    fontSize: { 'xs': '12px', 'md': '16px' },
    fontWeight: { 'normal': '400', 'bold': '700' },
    lineHeight: { 'md': '24px', '5xl': '1' },
    letterSpacing: { 'tight': '-0.025em' },
    boxShadow: { 'md': '0px 3px 4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1)', 'soft-1': '...' },
    zIndex: { 'modal': '2000', 'toast': '3000' },
    opacity: { 'faint': '0.08', 'muted': '0.4' },
    transitionDuration: { 'normal': '200ms' },
    transitionTimingFunction: { 'standard': 'cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)' },
  },
};
```

Adding a semantic colour = adding a `<role>` in **every** theme of
`themes.xml`; adding a scale = adding a `<value>` in `design/tokens.xml`. Then
run `npm run design:gen` and every utility (`bg-success`, `p-4`, `rounded-md`,
`shadow-hard-1`, `z-modal`, `ease-standard`, ...) exists.

The raw `color` palette is deliberately not injected into Tailwind: it is
internal, and only the semantic colours are meaningful as utilities.
